'''''Kalanchoe luciae''''', the '''paddle plant''' or '''flapjacks''', is a species of flowering plant in the genus ''[[Kalanchoe]]'', native to northeast [[South Africa]], [[Eswatini]], [[Mozambique]] and [[Zimbabwe]].<ref name="274396-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:274396-1 |title=''Kalanchoe luciae'' Raym.-Hamet |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2017 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=26 November 2020 }}</ref> It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=''Kalanchoe luciae'' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/327526/Kalanchoe-luciae/Details |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |accessdate=26 November 2020 }}</ref>

''K. luciae'' is often mistaken for a similar but rarely cultivated species, [[Kalanchoe thyrsiflora|''Kalanchoe'' ''thyrsiflora'']]. ''K. luciae'' has larger, more vibrant leaves and develops white flowers with no noticeable scent, while ''K. thyrsiflora'' has fragrant, yellow flowers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Flapjacks, Kalanchoe spp. |url=https://hort.extension.wisc.edu/articles/flapjacks-kalanchoe-spp/ |access-date=2023-03-30 |website=Wisconsin Horticulture |language=en-US}}</ref>
